questions.question: Which state of India has the longest mainland coastline?

questions.question: The term 'Dolphin Kick' is associated with which sport?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **The Dolphin kick is associated with the Swimming.**__
 
• The Dolphin kick technique is used by professional swimmers, they use that motion that propels them forward underwater after diving in, and at the underwater turns.
 
• This technique is not just about the legs but It requires a swimmer's entire body to crack like a whip, creating a fluid wave that starts at the chest and increases in amplitude as it travels all the way through the toes, and it seems like a dolphin that's why it is called **Dolphin kick**.
 
• The Dolphin Kick is assumed as the fastest way to get from one point to another underwater but it needs a lot of practice as it is a very difficult move.

 
• The international rules for swimming disciplines are laid down by Federation Internationale de Natation (International Swimming Federation) FINA.
 
• There are four standard strokes in swimming a front crawl, backstroke, breaststroke, and butterfly.

questions.question: Blue litmus paper turns __________ on contact with an acidic solution.
questions.solution:
__
 
• Litmus paper test is done to find whether a solution is Acidic or Basic in nature.
 
• Litmus paper is a type of pH paper made by treating paper with natural dyes from lichens.
 
• **The blue litmus paper turns red or pink when it comes into contact with an acidic solution of pH value below pH 4.5**__
 
• It becomes purple if the pH of the solution is between 4.5 and 8.3 and if the pH is above 8.3 it stays blue.
 
• The solution which is Basic in nature having a pH range between 8.5 and 14 changes the colour of red litmus paper to blue.

questions.question: During World War II, the Battles of Kohima and Imphal were fought in the year ________.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **The Battles of Kohima and Imphal were fought between 8 March and 18 July 1944.**__
 
• In 1944, during the rise of the Second World War, the Japanese forces attacked the northeast region of India through Burma. They attacked Imphal first and then they move towards Kohima the capital city of Nagaland.
 
• The British and Indian forces fought valiantly and prevented the ambitious plans of Japan, resulting in the fiercest battles of Kohima and Imphal.

**Extra Information :**

 
• World War II was a global war that lasted from 1939 to 1945.
 
• World War II was fought between two groups of countries one side was Germany with Italy and Japan and opposite side were Britain, France, Australia, Canada, New Zealand, India, the Soviet Union, China and the United States of America.
 
• World War II was started due to the invasion of Germany on Poland on September 1, 1939, then Britain and France responded to the Germany move and they declared war on Germany on September 3.
 
• The Battle of Stalingrad was the most important battle of World war II it was the bloodiest battle in history as it caused about two million casualties.

questions.question: In the year ________, the Maratha Empire ceased to exist with the surrender of the Marathas to the British, ending the Third Anglo-Maratha War.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **The Third Anglo-Maratha War ended in 1818 with the surrender of the Marathas to the British.**__
 
• The Third Anglo-Maratha War took place in Maharashtra and its neighboring areas in 1817 and 1818.
 
• The main reason for the Third Anglo-Maratha war was British conflict with the **Pindaris** whom the British suspected were being protected by the Marathas.
 
• The** Treaty of Mandasor** was signed between the British and the Holkar chief in 1818.
 
• Main reasons for the loss of Marathas were lack of unity among the Maratha chiefs themselves, lack of good relations with other Indian princes and ruling dynasties and failure to understand the British political and diplomatic strengths.

questions.question: Rajat has hypermetropia. What type of lens will the ophthalmologist recommend to correct his vision?
questions.solution:
__** Concept:**__

 
 

 
 
Defects of Vision

 
 
 
Details

 
 
 
Corrections

 
 
 

 
 
Hypermetropia or Farsightedness

 
 
 
The human eye can see distant objects clearly but cannot see nearby objects clearly.

 
 
 
Convex Lens

 
 
 

 
 
Presbyopia

 
 
 
In this defect both near and far objects are not clearly visible. It is an old age disease and it is due to the loosing power of accommodation.

 
 
 
Bifocal lenses

 
 
 

 
 
Astigmatism

 
 
 
In this defect, the eye cannot see horizontal and vertical lines clearly, simultaneously. It is due to the imperfect spherical nature of the eye lens.

 
 
 
Cylindrical lens

 
 
 

__**Explanation:**__

From the above explanation, we can see that,

 
• A person with hypermetropia can see distant objects clearly but cannot see nearby objects distinctly. 
 
• Hypermetropia is also known as **farsightedness. **Such a person has to keep a reading material much beyond 25 cm from the eye for comfortable reading.
 
• Hypermetropia defect can arise mainly due to two reasons (i) the focal length of the eye lens become too long or (ii) the eyeball becomes too small.
 
• This defect can be corrected by using a **convex lens of appropriate power.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ddaeecbae86655fba69b87bccaf1d4c88e99d10f96164728924c841fc6f89898.png] 

 
• A concave lens is used for the correction of Myopia which is also known as near-sightedness.
 
• The bifocal lens can be used for the correction of Presbyopia (a person suffering from both myopia and hypermetropia).
 
• Progressive lenses also called multifocal lenses are the lenses that have a seamless progression of added magnifying power for intermediate and near vision.

questions.question: A substantial increase in capital expenditure or revenue deficit leads to ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3 i.e. __**Fiscal Deficit.**__

 
• 
 
**Fiscal Deficit **is the sum of** revenue and capital expenditure minus(-) all revenue and capital received other than the loan is taken.** A substantial increase in **capital expenditure or revenue deficit leads to Fiscal Deficit**

 
 
• 
 
**Fiscal Deficit = Revenue Received + Capital Received - Total Expenditure**

 
 
• **Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure - Revenue Received**

 
• The **Primary deficit** is the fiscal deficit of the current year minus interest payments on previous borrowings.
 
• **Primary Deficit = fiscal Deficit - Interset Payment.**
 
• **Budgetary deficit** is the sum of deficits of the revenue and capital accounts.

questions.question: Name the tissue that transports food to various parts of a plant.
questions.solution:
__
 
• Phloem is a vascular tissue through which the food prepared by the leaves is transported to various organs of the plants.
 
• Phloem is a composition of four types of cells Sieve tubes, Companion cells, Pholeom parenchyma, and phloem fibers.
 
• Xylem is a water-conducting tissue of vascular plants which consists of dead hollow cells in the form of fibers and sclereids.
 
• Parenchyma are the simple permanent tissues whose cells are usually isodiametric but in various organs, due to pressure and surface tension of the neighborhood cells, their shapes sometimes change. These tissues store the foodstuffs and the parts of the leaf mesophyll, endosperms, fruit pulp etc are made from the parenchyma.
 
• Sclerenchyma are also the simple permanent tissues which are scattered in the organs of the plants to provide mechanical support and rigidity to the plant organs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: Who was the last ruler of the Vaghela Dynasty of Gujarat after whose defeat the kingdom was passed to Alauddin Khilji?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The** Vaghela dynasty** was an Indian dynasty that ruled Gujarat for a short time period in the13th century CE.
 
• The Vaghela's were the last Hindu kings to rule large parts of Gujarat, with capital **Dholka** before the Alauddin Khilji's army conquest of the region.
 
• **In 1304, a second attack by Alauddin's forces defeated Karandev, the last ruler of the Vaghela Dynasty of Gujarat and permanently ended the Vaghela dynasty**__. This resulted in the annexation of Gujarat to the Delhi Sultanate.
